QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_24

question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations and the 2021 amendment, which body's members 'shall be responsible for the decisions taken' in an AIF fund management organisation (unless the Large-Value-Fund / INR 70 cr waiver applies)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2021 (w.e.f. May 5, 2021), members of the Investment Committee are responsible for decisions taken and must ensure compliance with SEBI (AIF) Regulations. Exemption is available only for LVF / INR 70 cr-commitment investors who furnish a waiver. The Trap: The Advisory Committee, distributors and auditors are not decision-accountability bodies under the 2021 amendment. Cross-Exam Context: Same accountability rule in XIX-C/D. Distinguish IC (decision body) from Advisory Committee (non-binding recommendations). Manager's Pro-Tip: Secure D&O insurance for external IC members up to 2-3x their annual fees — the 2021 accountability rule puts them on the hook for SEBI actions, and without insurance protection, you'll struggle to recruit quality external members to a Cat III fund.
